_comment: Kelp Watch analysis polygons per docs/03. One Feature per area the analysis compares kelp over. Each declares polygon_id (the key every kelp and comparison row joins on), purpose (near_site, control or regional), site_ids (the stations this polygon is compared against, so no analysis code string-matches a polygon name), and source_file -- the Kelp Watch export its rows arrive in, because the CSV names the geometry it describes nowhere in the file (docs/02). kelp_watch pins the dataset revision the exports came from; bumping it obsoletes every landing at the old revision, because a newer revision may revise history as well as extend it. Geometry is WGS84 (RFC 7946) and is null here: these six are Kelp Watch's own named bed geometries, selected in the site's UI, and their outlines have not been recorded in this repository yet. Nothing computes from them -- the export arrives already summed over the selected geometry -- but docs/04 s4.5's distance-decay test will need them, and that is the stage that should refuse a polygon without one.
_provisional: The purpose labels and the site pairings below are a first pass and are meant to be revised. NDBC:LJAC1's published position (32.867, -117.257) is inside the La Jolla bed, so that bed is regional and the other five are controls. Every bed is paired with both public reference stations and both project sensors, which is the docs/04 s4.5 comparison; both project sites are now surveyed in sites.json, but a near_site polygon still cannot be declared: these six are Kelp Watch's own bed geometries and none of their outlines is recorded here, so what is missing is geometry, not position. SIO:LAJOLLA-PIER is paired at both of its sensor depths, 0.5 m and 5.0 m, rather than at one chosen here: they are independent series carrying independent coverage bookkeeping, docs/04 s4.1 is exploratory by decision, and whether a surface and a 5 m shore record behave differently against canopy is a question the screen answers rather than one to settle by assertion. It is a daily shore record from a different instrument than LJAC1's hourly hull sensor, so the two sit in one parameter column measuring the same quantity by different means; the screen reports them as separate series and never pools them. Adding a second public reference to all six beds widens the docs/04 s5 denominator, which is accepted: a screen cannot be told it is recovering seasonality by a reference it does not have. Changing any of this is a data(registry) edit needing no code.

kelp_watch._comment: From the export's own recommended-citation download, retrieved 2026-08-26: Bell, T., K. Cavanaugh, D. Siegel. 2024. SBC LTER: Time series of quarterly NetCDF files of kelp biomass in the canopy from Landsat 5, 7 and 8, since 1984 (ongoing) ver 23. Environmental Data Initiative.

properties.name: La Jolla kelp bed
properties.notes: The bed containing NDBC:LJAC1, whose published position sits inside it. Both project sensors are recorded as deployed in this bed, ~2.0 km from LJAC1. Their positions are now surveyed (sites.json), but this polygon has no geometry, so containment is taken from the deployment record rather than computed.

properties.name: Del Mar kelp bed
properties.notes: The smallest bed exported. Genuinely empty for most of the record, which makes it the bed where a fabricated cloud-gap zero would be least visible (docs/02).

properties.name: Encinitas kelp bed
properties.notes: The northern end of the exported range.

properties.name: San Diego kelp bed
properties.notes: The largest bed exported, by a factor of nearly two over La Jolla.

properties.name: Imperial Beach kelp bed
properties.notes: The southern end of the exported range.
